critic.content:
Your input fields are:
1. `setting` (str): The curriculum and country this pack is written for. Vocabulary normal in that setting is correct even where another one would say it differently.
2. `lesson_objective` (str): What this section is meant to teach.
3. `teaching_evidence` (str): What the class was taught, as recorded by the teacher. May be empty.
4. `section_to_review` (str): The section exactly as the learner reads it.
Your output fields are:
1. `reasoning` (str): 
2. `findings` (list[ContentFinding]): Every defect found, each quoting the section verbatim. Empty when there are none.
All interactions will be structured in the following way, with the appropriate values filled in.

[[ ## setting ## ]]
{setting}

[[ ## lesson_objective ## ]]
{lesson_objective}

[[ ## teaching_evidence ## ]]
{teaching_evidence}

[[ ## section_to_review ## ]]
{section_to_review}

[[ ## reasoning ## ]]
{reasoning}

[[ ## findings ## ]]
{findings}        # note: the value you produce must adhere to the JSON schema: {"type": "array", "$defs": {"ContentFinding": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "description": "One defect in a review-pack section, tied to the text that carries it.", "properties": {"defect": {"type": "string", "description": "Which kind of defect this is.", "enum": ["grounding", "consistency", "audience"], "title": "Defect"}, "problem": {"type": "string", "description": "What is wrong with them.", "minLength": 1, "title": "Problem"}, "quote": {"type": "string", "description": "The exact words from the section that carry the defect, copied verbatim.", "minLength": 1, "title": "Quote"}}, "required": ["defect", "quote", "problem"], "title": "ContentFinding"}}, "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/ContentFinding"}}

[[ ## completed ## ]]
In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Find text in a review-pack section that must not reach a learner.
        
        Read the section as the 11-to-13 year old it is written for. Report a
        finding only where you can quote the exact words that carry the defect, and
        only for these three kinds:
        
        grounding — something stated as fact that is false or unfounded: a wrong
          definition or rule, a claim about real events or people that never
          happened, a cause or reason invented to explain the numbers, or material
          from a topic this lesson did not cover. Made-up numbers in an example or
          practice question are ordinary teaching and are NOT a defect; what must
          never be invented is an explanation OF them, or a fact about the world.
          Teaching the lesson's own topic is what the section is FOR, so standard
          definitions, explanations and extra practice belong in it whether or not
          the evidence spells them out. Anything the evidence itself states is
          settled — this class was taught it, so never report it, and never correct
          it towards a more general or more advanced formulation. Report invention,
          never elaboration.
        consistency — a statement the section's own tables, numbers or examples
          contradict, or a worked answer that does not follow from its own working.
        audience — text written for anyone other than the learner: labels naming
          the lesson's own stages or objectives, narration of what the teacher does
          in class, or any mention of where the material came from ("the source",
          "the textbook", "the evidence", "the lesson note"). Numbered steps inside
          a worked solution or instructions to the reader are how a method is taught
          and are NOT a defect.
        
        Work through the section to the end and report every defect you find. Report
        nothing about style, tone, length or how much of the objective is covered.
        Return an empty list when the section is clean.

[[ ## setting ## ]]
JSS1, the Nigerian UBE junior secondary (NERDC) mathematics curriculum

[[ ## lesson_objective ## ]]
Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle.

[[ ## teaching_evidence ## ]]
Perimeter is the total distance round a closed shape.
For a rectangle of length L and breadth B, perimeter = 2(L + B).
Example: L = 8 cm, B = 5 cm, perimeter = 2(8 + 5) = 26 cm.

[[ ## section_to_review ## ]]
Distance round a rectangle

The perimeter of a rectangle is 2 x (length + breadth).

A rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm has perimeter 2 x (8 + 5) = 26 cm.

Find the perimeter of a rectangle 7 cm by 4 cm.

22 cm

2 x (7 + 4) = 2 x 11 = 22 cm.

Respond with the corresponding output fields, starting with the field `[[ ## reasoning ## ]]`, then `[[ ## findings ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python list[ContentFinding]), and then ending with the marker for `[[ ## completed ## ]]`.

repair.content:
Your input fields are:
1. `policy` (GenerationPolicyContext): 
2. `lesson_context` (dict): 
3. `unit_context` (dict): The lesson objective this section teaches, and how the lesson taught it.
4. `source_evidence` (list[dict]): 
5. `failed_section` (dict): The section to fix. Return it with the smallest possible edit. Its figures are attached separately and are not shown or returned here.
6. `validation_issues` (list[str]): The exact problems to fix; any phrase quoted here must NOT appear in the repaired section.
Your output fields are:
1. `reasoning` (str): 
2. `repaired_section` (RevisedSection): The same section with only the offending text changed.
All interactions will be structured in the following way, with the appropriate values filled in.

[[ ## policy ## ]]
{policy}

[[ ## lesson_context ## ]]
{lesson_context}

[[ ## unit_context ## ]]
{unit_context}

[[ ## source_evidence ## ]]
{source_evidence}

[[ ## failed_section ## ]]
{failed_section}

[[ ## validation_issues ## ]]
{validation_issues}

[[ ## reasoning ## ]]
{reasoning}

[[ ## repaired_section ## ]]
{repaired_section}        # note: the value you produce must adhere to the JSON schema: {"type": "object", "$defs": {"DraftBlock": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "description": "One model-authored prose block, without record identity or provenance.", "properties": {"block_type": {"type": "string", "description": "What this block is for the reader.", "enum": ["explanation", "worked_example"], "title": "Block Type"}, "text": {"type": "string", "description": "The block, written for the reader.", "title": "Text"}}, "required": ["block_type", "text"], "title": "DraftBlock"}, "DraftPractice": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "description": "One model-authored practice item, without its persisted id.", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "description": "What the learner checks against, after attempting.", "title": "Answer"}, "prompt": {"type": "string", "description": "The question, as the learner reads it.", "title": "Prompt"}, "worked_solution": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "description": "The steps to the answer, where the answer alone will not do.", "title": "Worked Solution"}}, "required": ["prompt", "answer"], "title": "DraftPractice"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "description": "A finished section as the model reworks it, without persisted record fields.", "properties": {"blocks": {"type": "array", "description": "The instructional blocks, in the order the reader meets them.", "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DraftBlock"}, "title": "Blocks"}, "practice": {"type": "array", "description": "What the learner does, each with the answer they check against.", "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DraftPractice"}, "title": "Practice"}, "title": {"type": "string", "description": "The reader-facing section title.", "title": "Title"}}, "required": ["title", "blocks"], "title": "RevisedSection"}

[[ ## completed ## ]]
In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Repair a review-pack section that failed deterministic validation.
        
        Make the SMALLEST edit that fixes exactly the issues listed in
        validation_issues: delete or rewrite only the offending text and keep every
        other sentence and block exactly as it is, in the same order. Keep the same
        lesson objective. When an issue quotes a phrase, that phrase must not appear
        in the repaired section. Never add new claims about where content came from.
